author: Dave Jensen
title: 2 Local Smashburger Spots Close - NewsBreak
text:
By Dave Jensen ,
12 hours ago
Burger lovers in Colorado may have noticed that a couple of Smashburgers in Northern Colorado had ceased to exist by end of August of 2025.
Mile High City Welcomed the Very First Smashburger The Smashburger chain got its start in Denver in 2007. The founders created their own “smasher” for burgers; they quickly took off, opening more and more locations. Two of those locations, one in Longmont, one in Loveland, are no longer open.
Smashburger is interesting in the fact that it’s a fast-casual burger joint where, at select locations, you can get alcoholic drinks. I know I stopped at the Loveland location a couple of times, for a “burger, beer and fries.”
Loveland Burger Joint Sees Opportunity with Loss of Smashburger Loveland’s Smashburger location opened in in the summer of 2011, at Eisenhower Boulevard and Denver Avenue. It was a fairly good location, as there aren’t a lot of burger joints near there. There is a Fat Shack a few doors down, however, and they were quick to try and get some sad Smashburger lovers to head their way.
TSM/Dave Jensen It was in late 2023, that In-N-Out came to Loveland, about two miles away form Smashburger, near the interstate, at Centerra. It’s hard to say how that may have affected Smashburger, but people sure do love In-N-Out, even without having alcohol.
READ MORE: That Time a Fight Broke Out at Loveland’s Smashburger Over Bathroom Etiquette .
Longmont’s location opened in the summer of 2013, at Hover Street and Nelson Road in early 2013. There is a lot of competition for diners in that area, including how In-N-Out is planned for Longmont , near the city’s Costco.
Fort Collins’ Smashburger, off of Harmony and Snow Mesa, is one of the 21 remaining Colorado locations as of September 2025.
Google Street View Chains That Are Closing or Have Closed Locations in 2025 The list of chains that have closed locations or have plans to shutter stores later in 2025 continues to grow at a rapid pace. Gallery Credit: Rob Carroll Getty Images Advance Auto Parts Advance Auto Parts is more or less reshuffling the deck on its stores. The company announced in late 2024 that it is rolling out a " strategic plan " to reduce the number of its properties.
This includes: Closing 523 Advance Auto Parts corporate stores Exiting 204 independent locations Closing four distribution centers An exact timeline for the company to enact the plan as not yet been announced. We do know Advance is targeting having its distribution centers consolidated into "13 large facilities" by 2026.
Getty Images Amazon Fresh Amazon two different brick-and-mortar stores. Amazon Go is a convenience store with grab-and-go items. Amazon Fresh serves as more of a grocery store.
The company recently announced the closing of some Amazon Fresh locations in California and Virginia after deciding the format may not have been right for those areas.
Amazon also whittled down its Go store portfolio in 2024. Getty Images At Home Home decor and furniture retailer At Home announced in June that it had entered chapter 11 bankruptcy protection. As part of the move, the company plans to close as many as 26 stores before the end of September. Getty Images Best Buy Best Buy has been slowly closing locations for a while now. It just hasn't made much of a splash since they didn't all close at the same time.
Money Digest reported back in February 2024 that Best Buy had plans to close 24 stores during the year with another 10 to 15 stores shuttering in 2025. Getty Images Big Lots Big Lots was acquired out of bankruptcy court at the last minute to start the year. Several locations have already closed, but there is a chance others may survive after all.
Business of Home reports some locations will continue to carry Big Lots branding while others will be retooled to be "less furniture-centric" and possibly go by a different name,
Getty Images Claire's Claire's announced plans filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy this summer. Just a couple weeks later, it was announced the chain would be potentially sold to a private equity firm.
ChainStoreAge.com reported at the end of August that 235 Claire's stores had been targeted for closure. Another 56 locations branded as Icing stores will also close. Getty Images CosMc's McDonald's will reportedly close three locations occupied by its spinoff restaurant, CosMc's . The brand's menu focuses heavily on drinks with a smaller food menu featuring quick bites.
While three locations may be closing, additional CosMc's in smaller buildings are planned to open in 2025. Getty Images Del Taco A Del Taco franchisee closed 18 of its restaurant locations in Colorado in February following a bankruptcy filing. The closings left one remaining Del Taco open in the state. Getty Images Denny's On its website, the Denny's Corporation boasts that it is "one of the largest full-service restaurant chains based on number of restaurants."
The chain was on track to close 50 restaurants by the end of 2024. Another 100 locations have been marked for closing sometime in 2025. Getty Images Dick's Sporting Goods It's not "game over" for Dick's Sporting Goods, but some of its locations could be going away in 2025.
A report from Patch.com revealed 35 Dick's Sporting Goods stores are planned to close this year. Getty Images Dollar General Discount retailer Dollar General started the year on a fairly down note. In January, the chain closed 27 locations while opening up another nine stores.
The company says higher operating costs are to blame for the closures. Getty Images Domino's The news of Domino's closing locations will hit differently depending on your home country.
The pizza chain is planning to close up to 205 locations in 2025. For now, most of those are outside the U.S. with at least 170 located in Japan. Getty Images Foot Locker It's a story of both closings and openings for Foot Locker. ABC News reports the chain will close more than 400 stores by 2026.
At the same time, Foot Locker has plans to rebrand some of its locations. Long-time footwear source will retool 280 stores that "focus on its community, power store and play concepts." Getty Images Forever 21 Forever 21 started closing select underperforming stores in February with plans to close as many as 200 locations. Getty Images Goodwill Goodwill announced in April that it would close 13 locations, all in California. The locations are a mix of stores and donation sites. Getty Images Jack In the Box Following a year of plummeting stock prices, Jack In The Box closed a handful of underperforming stores in February . The chain has nearly 2,200 locations scattered across 22 states. Andriy Blokhin // Shutterstock JCPenney JCPenney began the first quarter of 2025 by announcing plans to close eight stores . The company had previously filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection. Those stores were shut down for good in May. Google Maps image JoAnn JoAnn announced in February the company would close all of its remaining stores following its second bankruptcy filing in less than a year. Getty Images Kirkland's Home decor chain Kirkland's, which operates around 300 stores in 35 states, recently purchased the Bed, Bath and Beyond brand in hopes of refocusing its strategy.
Part of that strategy will be shedding underperforming stores while also converting some locations to brands that could potentially increase profit. Getty Images Kohl's Department store retailer Kohl's has been shedding some of its stores in 2025.
Coming into the year, the chain had more than 1,150 locations. ChainStoreAge.com reported Kohl's plans to close 27 "underperforming stores" and a fulfillment center before April. Getty Images Kroger Grocery store chain Kroger announced in June that it will close as many as 60 underperforming locations before the end of 2026. Locations targeted for closure include stores in Illinois, Georgia, Texas and Virginia. Getty Images Lumber Liquidators/LL Flooring LL Flooring, previously known as Lumber Liquidators, was ready to close for good until it was acquired by a private equity firm in late 2024.
Retail Dive reports nearly 100 stores were slated to close as part of the company's Chapter 11 filing. Getty Images Macy's Macy's announced in mid-2024 that it would close 150 locations in a span of two years. Unfortunately, that timeline seems to have accelerated.
Initial plans called for closing 50 stores by the end of January 2025. That number has now been bumped up to 65 . Getty Images Noodles & Company In 2024, Noodles & Company closed as many as 20 locations to cut down on high operating losses. The same thing is happening in 2025 with 17 locations reportedly marked for closure. Google Maps On The Border Tex-Mex chain On The Border closed nearly a third of its 120 restaurants in late February. Just weeks later, it was reported the company had filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy.
In addition to its restaurants, On The Border also sells a line of branded retail products including chips and salsas that can be found in stores throughout the U.S. Getty Images Party City Party City isn't just closing locations, it is going away for good in 2025. The store's parent company announced in December of 2024 every Party City will be closed as of Feb. 28 . Getty Images PNC Bank Less than two years ago, PNC Bank closed nearly 10% of its branches. Additional locations were shuttered in 2025 with branches disappearing in Texas, Illinois, New Jersey, Wisconsin and Ohio Getty Images Red Robin It may take some time. but burger chain Red Robin is planning to close as many as 70 locations . It all starts this year with 10-15 underperforming restaurants shutting down for goos. Google Maps image Smokey Bones Bar and Fire Grills Smokey Bones announced in March that it was planning to close at least nine underperforming locations. Half of its remaining locations will also be transitioned into the Twin Peaks brand. Getty Images 7-Eleven While plans to close more than 400 stores seems shocking, it doesn't make much of a dent in 7-Eleven's overall store count.
The convenience store announced in 2024 that it would begin the process of closing 444 of its more than 13,000 locations in North America after sales have " sharply declined. "
Additional 7-Eleven locations may be getting a facelift to offer higher-quality food offerings that are often found in the chain's Japanese stores . Getty Images TGI Fridays There was a lot going on with TGI Fridays just in the first month of 2025.
Eat This, Not That! reported the chain was set to close 36 locations in January alone. On top of that, the company announced plans to sell off nine of its restaurants. Getty Images Torrid The women's apparel chain informed investors in March that it would begin its store "optimization" plan . As many as 50 stores will reportedly close before the end of the year. Other locations will receive makeovers. Getty Images UPS It was reported in May that United Parcel Service, better known as UPS, would be closing as many as 73 leased or owned buildings before July 1. The company will also reportedly cut nearly 20,000 jobs as part of the process. Getty Images Walgreens Drugstores have been rapidly closing in recent years with Rite-Aid and CVS hit hard in 2024.
Walgreens is no different. Good Housekeeping reports Walgreens is closing 2,150 locations between now and 2027, accounting for nearly a quarter of its 8,600 stores. Sundry Photography // Shutterstock Walmart Walmart will reportedly close stores in six different states in 2025. Among the states affected by the closures, California will likely be hit the hardest with six Walmart locations on the chopping block.
